tier_rationale: Anova's own product page states the device is operated 'with the controls or the app' and describes a two-line touchscreen that sets time and temperature and starts a cook directly on the unit. A vendor cloud plainly exists and is nameable: the Anova Culinary app connects to Anova's own cloud for remote monitoring/control, and Anova's 2024 subscription FAQ describes an account-gated tier of that same app. Core function — heating water to a set temperature for a set time — runs entirely on-device with no app, no account and no network. What the subscription and account gate is app-only: recipe discovery, cook history, and remote start/monitor from a phone.
the_unplug_test: You set time and temperature on the cooker's own touchscreen and press start; it heats the water bath and runs the cook with no WiFi, no app and no account, exactly as it would connected. What you lose without the cloud: starting or checking a cook from your phone, Anova's recipe library, cook history, and (for anyone who did not have an Anova account before 21 August 2024) those app features sit behind a $2/month or $10/year subscription. None of that touches the physical cook.
offline_losses: starting or monitoring a cook from the Anova Culinary app
Anova's recipe library and cook history
for accounts created on or after 2024-08-21, app access at all requires a paid subscription ($2/mo or $10/yr) — pre-existing accounts were grandfathered free

Two dated incidents worth a human review: (1) 2024-08-14 announced / 2024-08-21 effective — Anova introduced a $2/mo or $10/yr subscription gating app remote-control and monitoring for any account created from that date forward; accounts existing before the cutoff were grandfathered free (source: Engadget, 2024-08). (2) Simultaneously with (1), Anova announced it would end app/cloud connectivity support entirely for its original first-generation Precision Cooker (Bluetooth-only and Bluetooth+WiFi models), effective September 2025 — a real 'shipped device loses function' plan. Anova reversed this on 2025-01-16 after owner backlash and committed to indefinite support for all versions instead (source: Anova's own blog post 'Good news about ongoing product support', updated 2025-01-16; corroborated independently by a Home Assistant community thread dated 2024-09 through 2025). Net effect: a real, dated threat to already-sold hardware that did not materialize. This looks like a disputed-but-partially-established pattern (ledger scale '1'), not a '2', because the harmful action was announced and then withdrawn before taking effect — but the subscription-for-new-accounts change did take effect and stands today.
